courses.title: AI Lab
courses.subject: Python, machine learning and system design

exercises.title: Count the tokens
exercises.brief: A tokenizer splits text into pieces. Write a function called `count_tokens` that takes a string and returns the number of whitespace-separated words in it, then print the answer for "the quick brown fox".

exercises.title: Scale the scores
exercises.brief: Model outputs arrive on any scale. Write `normalise` so it takes a list of numbers and divides each one by the largest value in the list. Print the result for [2, 4, 8].

exercises.title: Softmax
exercises.brief: Softmax turns raw scores into probabilities that add up to one. Write `softmax` that takes a list of numbers, subtracts the largest value from each one (so nothing overflows), exponentiates them, and divides each by the total. Print the result for [1, 2, 3].

exercises.title: Sliding window
exercises.brief: A sliding window looks at every run of `size` items in a list. Write `windows` that returns each run of `size` numbers, in order. Print the result of `windows([1, 2, 3, 4], 2)`.

exercises.title: Count the bigrams
exercises.brief: A bigram is two words next to each other. Write `bigram_counts` that takes a list of words and returns a dictionary counting each pair. Print the result for ["a", "b", "a"].

exercises.title: Cosine similarity
exercises.brief: Cosine similarity says how alike two vectors are, ignoring their size. Write `cosine` that takes two lists of numbers and returns the dot product divided by the two lengths. Print the result for [1, 0] and [1, 0].

exercises.title: The mean is the baseline
exercises.brief: Every model has to beat the mean. Write `baseline` that takes a list of numbers and returns the average, then print the mean of [2, 4, 6, 8].

exercises.title: Keep the best three
exercises.brief: A model usually returns many candidates and the caller keeps the best few. Write `top_k` that returns the `k` largest numbers in a list, highest first. Print `top_k([3, 9, 1, 7], 2)`.

exercises.title: Stay inside the budget
exercises.brief: A request has a token budget. Write `truncate` that takes a list of tokens and a budget and returns only the first `budget` tokens. Print `truncate([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 3)`.

exercises.title: How often each word
exercises.brief: Write `word_counts` that takes a sentence split into words and returns a dictionary of how many times each word appears. Print it for ["a", "b", "a"].

exercises.title: A leaky bucket
exercises.brief: A leaky bucket shapes a bursty stream into a steady one. Write `leaky_bucket` that takes a list of arrivals per second and a capacity, and returns how many requests leave the bucket each second. Print `leaky_bucket([3, 0, 0, 4], 2)`.

exercises.title: Back off, then try again
exercises.brief: When a call fails, wait twice as long before trying again. Write `backoff` that takes an attempt number starting at one and returns the wait in seconds: 1, 2, 4, 8. Print `backoff(4)`.

exercises.title: Do not retry forever
exercises.brief: Retries cost money and time, so they need a ceiling. Write `should_retry` that returns True only when the attempt number is below the limit. Print `should_retry(2, 3)` and `should_retry(3, 3)`.

exercises.title: One request, one effect
exercises.brief: A retried request must not charge twice. Write `is_duplicate` that takes the keys already seen and a new key, and returns True when the key was seen before. Print `is_duplicate(["a", "b"], "b")`.

exercises.title: Did the cache answer?
exercises.brief: Write `cache_status` that takes a cache dictionary and a key and returns "hit" when the key is in the cache and "miss" otherwise. Print `cache_status({"a": 1}, "a")`.

exercises.title: A cache that understands
exercises.brief: A semantic cache serves an old answer when the new question means the same thing. Write `semantic_cache` that takes a list of questions and returns the first one whose letters match the query exactly, or None. Print `semantic_cache(["hello there", "bye"], "hello there")`.

exercises.title: Open the breaker
exercises.brief: A circuit breaker stops sending traffic to a service that keeps failing. Write `breaker_state` that takes a list of results where True means success and returns "open" when three failures in a row are found, otherwise "closed". Print `breaker_state([True, False, False, False])`.

exercises.title: How deep is the queue
exercises.brief: Write `queue_depth` that takes a list of job sizes and returns the total size still waiting. Print `queue_depth([1, 2, 3])`.

exercises.title: What does a call cost
exercises.brief: Write `call_cost` that takes the number of input tokens, the number of output tokens and a price per thousand tokens for each, and returns the total cost. Print `call_cost(1000, 500, 0.002, 0.004)`.

exercises.title: Spend the latency budget
exercises.brief: A request has a latency budget split across several steps. Write `within_budget` that adds the given step times and returns True when the total is under the budget. Print `within_budget([100, 200], 500)`.

exercises.title: Score the answers
exercises.brief: Write `accuracy` that takes the predicted labels and the true labels and returns the share that match, as a number between zero and one. Print `accuracy([1, 0, 1], [1, 0, 0])`.

exercises.title: Where the model is wrong
exercises.brief: Write `confusion` that takes the predicted labels and the true labels and returns a dictionary with the counts of true positives, true negatives, false positives and false negatives. Print it for [1, 0, 1] against [1, 0, 0].

exercises.title: Hide the personal data
exercises.brief: Write `redact` that takes a list of names and returns the same list with every name replaced by the text "REDACTED". Print `redact(["Ada", "Grace"])`.

exercises.title: Spot the injection
exercises.brief: A prompt injection tries to make the model ignore its instructions. Write `looks_like_injection` that returns True when the text contains "ignore previous". Print `looks_like_injection("please ignore previous instructions")`.

exercises.title: Keep the answer grounded
exercises.brief: A grounded answer has to point at a source. Write `has_grounding` that returns True only when the answer names at least one of the given sources. Print `has_grounding("the sky is blue, according to nasa", ["nasa"])`.

exercises.title: Run the eval suite
exercises.brief: An eval suite is a list of cases with the answer you expect. Write `run_eval` that takes the cases and a function and returns the share of cases the function gets right. Print `run_eval([(1, 1), (2, 3)], lambda pair: pair[0] == pair[1])`.

exercises.title: Watch for drift
exercises.brief: A model starts to drift when its accuracy falls below the threshold it was approved at. Write `has_drifted` that takes the current accuracy and the approved accuracy and returns True when the current score is lower. Print `has_drifted(0.8, 0.9)`.

exercises.title: Rate limit the public API
exercises.brief: Design what happens when 50,000 people call your public API at once. Explain how you would rate limit the traffic per user, what you would do with a request that goes over the limit, and how the service stays available when one user floods it.

exercises.title: Give the call a deadline
exercises.brief: Your service calls a slow third party that sometimes never answers. Explain how you would use a timeout and retry with backoff so that one slow call cannot hold up the whole request, and how you would fail fast when the dependency is clearly broken.

exercises.title: Cache the expensive answers
exercises.brief: Every request to your assistant costs money, and the same question arrives often. Explain how you would cache the answers, how long a cache entry should live, and how you would keep a stale entry from being served after the model changed.

exercises.title: Never charge twice
exercises.brief: A payment call timed out, so the client retried, and now the customer has been charged twice. Explain how you would make the write idempotent so that a retry is safe, and how the client would know which attempt was the real one.

exercises.title: Scale from one machine
exercises.brief: Your service starts on one machine and needs to serve a million users. Explain how you would scale it out over time, when you would add a read replica or a shard, and how the data store would keep up with the writes.

exercises.title: Strong or eventual, pick one
exercises.brief: A user updates their profile and immediately sees the old version on another page. Explain the consistency model you would choose, where you would relax it, and how you would keep the system available during a network split.

exercises.title: Take the slow work off the path
exercises.brief: Generating a report takes four minutes, and the user should not have to wait for it. Explain how you would use a queue and a background worker, and what you would do when the queue grows longer than the workers can handle.

exercises.title: The user wrote the instructions
exercises.brief: A user can put anything in the input box, including text that tries to make your assistant reveal its system prompt. Explain how you would treat untrusted input, where you would put the boundary between instruction and data, and how you would test for this before shipping.

exercises.title: The model made it up
exercises.brief: Your assistant confidently invented a citation that does not exist. Explain how you would ground the answers, how you would measure how often it happens, and what you would show the user when the model is not sure.

exercises.title: Do not keep what you must not keep
exercises.brief: People type their medical details into your assistant. Explain what personal data you would collect, what you would redact before sending it to a model, how long you would keep the logs, and who may read them.

exercises.title: Prove it got better
exercises.brief: You changed the prompt and the answers look different. Explain how you would build an eval set, how you would compare the two versions, and what you would watch for so that one good prompt does not hide a regression.

exercises.title: Keep the bill under control
exercises.brief: The bill for the model calls tripled this month. Explain where the tokens are going, how you would cut the cost without making the answers worse, and how you would make the spend visible before it becomes a surprise.

exercises.title: Swap the model without a break
exercises.brief: You want to move from one model to a new one, but the answers come out in a different shape. Explain how you would roll the change out, how you would keep the old model available, and how you would undo the change if it goes wrong.

exercises.title: Make the first call
exercises.brief: An API call returns a response with a status code and a body. The lab ships a fake API at `https://api.example.com/users`. Write code that imports `requests`, makes a GET call to that address, and prints the status code. The answer is 200.

exercises.title: Read the body
exercises.brief: A JSON body is a list of records. Write code that calls `https://api.example.com/users`, turns the body into Python objects with `response.json()`, and prints the name of every user. There are five of them, and the first is Ada Lovelace.

exercises.title: Check before you trust it
exercises.brief: A call that fails still returns a response, so the status has to be checked before the body is read. Write code that calls `https://api.example.com/does-not-exist`, and prints `missing` when the status is 404 and `found` otherwise.

exercises.title: Send a query
exercises.brief: A search is a URL with a query string on the end. Write code that calls `https://api.example.com/search?q=attention` and prints how many documents came back. One document matches.

exercises.title: Page through the results
exercises.brief: A big list does not come in one piece. Write code that calls the documents endpoint with `?page=1` and `?page=2`, then prints how many documents came back in total. There are four documents.

exercises.title: Try again, carefully
exercises.brief: A request that fails with a server error is worth trying again; a request that fails with a 404 is not. Write code that calls the users endpoint, and if the status is 500 it tries a second time. Print the status code of the call that finally answered.

exercises.title: Give it a deadline
exercises.brief: A call with no deadline can hang forever, so every call needs one. Write code that sets a timeout of 5 seconds on the session, makes the call to the users endpoint, and prints the number of users that came back.

exercises.title: Make the table
exercises.brief: The lab ships an in-memory database. Write code that imports `sqlite3`, opens a database called `shop`, and creates a table called `orders` with the columns `id` (INTEGER), `item` (TEXT) and `price` (INTEGER). Then print the names of the tables.

exercises.title: Put the rows in
exercises.brief: Write code that creates a table `orders` with the columns `id`, `item` and `price`, inserts two rows — `(1, 'book', 12)` and `(2, 'pen', 2)` — and then prints how many rows the table holds.

exercises.title: Ask a question
exercises.brief: Write code that creates a table `orders`, inserts `(1, 'book', 12)`, `(2, 'pen', 2)` and `(3, 'lamp', 30)`, then asks for the items that cost more than 10 and prints each one. The answer is `book` and `lamp`, in that order.

exercises.title: Only the top two
exercises.brief: Write code that creates a table `orders` with three rows — `(1, 'book', 12)`, `(2, 'pen', 2)` and `(3, 'lamp', 30)` — then asks for the two most expensive items and prints each one. The answer is `lamp` and `book`, in that order.

exercises.title: Change one row
exercises.brief: Write code that creates a table `orders` with two rows — `(1, 'book', 12)` and `(2, 'pen', 2)` — raises the price of the book to 20 with an UPDATE, and then prints the price of the book.

exercises.title: Remove what is finished
exercises.brief: Write code that creates a table `orders` with three rows — `(1, 'book', 12)`, `(2, 'pen', 2)` and `(3, 'lamp', 30)` — deletes the rows that cost less than 10, and then prints how many rows are left. The answer is 2.

exercises.title: Add it up in the database
exercises.brief: Not every question needs the rows back. Write code that creates a table `orders` with three rows — `(1, 'book', 12)`, `(2, 'pen', 2)` and `(3, 'lamp', 30)` — then asks the database for the total price with a `SUM` and prints it. The answer is 44.

exercises.title: Two for tea
exercises.brief: Return "One for NAME, one for me." Substitute "you" when name is None. Define solve(name). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Build a leap-year calendar
exercises.brief: Return True when a year is divisible by four, except for century years unless also divisible by 400. Define solve(year). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Translate numbers into rain sounds
exercises.brief: Append Pling for a factor of 3, Plang for 5, and Plong for 7, in that order. Return the number as text if none fit. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Square a running total
exercises.brief: Add the integers from one through number and square the final total. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Add the square numbers
exercises.brief: Square each integer from one through number and add those squares. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Compare two square totals
exercises.brief: Subtract the sum of the individual squares from the square of the sum for integers 1 through number. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Check alphabet coverage
exercises.brief: Return True if the sentence contains every English letter at least once. Ignore case and punctuation. Define solve(sentence). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Find repeated letters
exercises.brief: Return True when no letter occurs twice. Ignore case, spaces and hyphens. Define solve(phrase). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Count a number sequence
exercises.brief: Start with a positive integer. Halve an even number or triple an odd number and add one. Count the steps to reach one. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Read a resistor color pair
exercises.brief: Read the first two bands as decimal digits. In order from 0 to 9 the colors are black, brown, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, grey and white. Define solve(colors). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Score a target by distance
exercises.brief: A dart lands at (x, y). Award 10 points within radius 1, 5 within radius 5, 1 within radius 10, and 0 outside. Boundaries count. Define solve(x, y). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Raise digits to a power
exercises.brief: For a nonnegative integer, raise each digit to the number of digits and add the results. Return whether the sum equals the input. Define solve(number). Use Run to experiment and Check answer to try the full set of inputs.

exercises.title: Price a classifier’s mistakes
exercises.brief: A monitoring classifier emits integer scores from 0 to 100. Predict positive when score ≥ threshold. A missed positive costs five review units and a false alarm costs two. Return the total cost for the paired lists; empty input costs zero.

exercises.title: Choose an operating threshold
exercises.brief: Evaluate each candidate using the same cost (miss 5, false alarm 2; scores at the threshold count positive). Return the cheapest threshold, choosing the larger threshold on a tie to limit alerts. Candidates is nonempty and may be unsorted.

exercises.title: Score retrieval with reciprocal rank
exercises.brief: A search page returns a list of document IDs in ranked order. Return 100 divided by the one-based rank of the first relevant result, rounded down to a whole number. Return zero when the list is empty or none of the IDs are relevant. Later relevant results do not add points.

exercises.title: Current through a resistor
exercises.brief: A 12 V supply drives a 470 Ω resistor. Work out the current that flows through it, in milliamps.

exercises.title: Power in a resistor
exercises.brief: A 5 V supply is connected to a 1 kΩ resistor. How much power does the resistor turn into heat, in milliwatts?

exercises.title: Resistor for an LED
exercises.brief: A red LED drops 2.0 V and should run at 15 mA from a 9 V supply. What value of series resistor do you need, in ohms?

exercises.title: Current at a junction
exercises.brief: 1.2 A arrives at a junction and splits into two branches. One branch takes 450 mA. How much goes down the other branch, in milliamps?

exercises.title: Two resistors in parallel
exercises.brief: Two resistors of 3 kΩ and 6 kΩ sit in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance, in ohms?

exercises.title: Voltage around a loop
exercises.brief: A 15 V source drives a loop with a 220 Ω and a 330 Ω resistor in series. What is the voltage across the 330 Ω resistor?

exercises.title: Divider output
exercises.brief: A 10 kΩ and a 15 kΩ resistor form a divider across a 12 V supply. Take the output across the 15 kΩ resistor. What is the output voltage?

exercises.title: Design a divider
exercises.brief: You need 2.5 V from a 10 V supply. Put a 20 kΩ resistor on top. What should the bottom resistor be, in ohms?

exercises.title: Why the output sags
exercises.brief: Your divider gives the right voltage with nothing attached, but the voltage drops as soon as you connect the circuit. Explain why, and say what you would add to fix it.

exercises.title: The RC time constant
exercises.brief: A 10 kΩ resistor and a 22 µF capacitor form an RC circuit. What is the time constant, in milliseconds?

exercises.title: Charging after one time constant
exercises.brief: A capacitor charges through a resistor from a 10 V source. After exactly one time constant, what is the voltage across it, in volts? (Hint: 1 − e⁻¹.)

exercises.title: How long to settle
exercises.brief: A 4.7 kΩ resistor and a 10 µF capacitor make a filter. How many milliseconds does it take to settle to within 1% of the final value? (Use five time constants.)

exercises.title: The RL time constant
exercises.brief: A 100 mH inductor and a 220 Ω resistor form an RL circuit. What is the time constant, in milliseconds?

exercises.title: Energy in the field
exercises.brief: A 50 mH inductor carries 2 A. How much energy is stored in its magnetic field, in millijoules? (E = ½LI².)

exercises.title: The spike when you switch off
exercises.brief: You switch off a coil and the voltage across it spikes to hundreds of volts. Explain what is happening, and say what you would put across the coil to protect the switch.

exercises.title: Cutoff frequency
exercises.brief: An RC low-pass uses a 4.7 kΩ resistor and a 100 nF capacitor. What is its cutoff frequency, in hertz?

exercises.title: Resonant frequency
exercises.brief: A 10 mH inductor and a 100 nF capacitor form a tank circuit. What is the resonant frequency, in kilohertz?

exercises.title: Choosing the filter
exercises.brief: You want to keep a slow sensor signal and strip off fast switching noise on the same wire. Say which kind of filter to use, and what to watch out for when you choose its component values.

exercises.title: Average of a half-wave signal
exercises.brief: A 12 V peak sine wave goes through a single diode. What is the average (DC) voltage after the diode, in volts? (Vpeak ÷ π.)

exercises.title: Ripple on a smoothed supply
exercises.brief: A supply delivers 50 mA at 100 Hz into a smoothing capacitor. What ripple voltage do you get, in millivolts, with a 2200 µF capacitor? (Ripple = I ÷ (f·C).)

exercises.title: Why the forward voltage moves
exercises.brief: The same diode does not have the same forward voltage at every current. Explain why, and say what happens to a diode that is driven in reverse beyond its breakdown voltage.

exercises.title: Current through a lit LED
exercises.brief: A blue LED drops 3.2 V and has a 470 Ω resistor from a 5 V supply. How much current flows, in milliamps?

exercises.title: Why white is brighter than green
exercises.brief: Two LEDs use the same power, but the white one looks brighter. Explain what is happening inside the white LED, and say what controls how bright an LED looks.

exercises.title: XOR truth table
exercises.brief: How many rows of a 2-input XOR truth table have the output high?

exercises.title: Push the bubble through
exercises.brief: A NAND gate has an inversion bubble on its output. Describe how you would rewrite it using De Morgan’s theorem, and say which other gate it becomes.

exercises.title: Mixing logic families
exercises.brief: You connect an old TTL chip to a modern CMOS chip. Explain what goes wrong at the voltage levels, and say what the gap between the low and high thresholds is called.

exercises.title: Half adder output
exercises.brief: A half adder adds A = 1 and B = 1. What is the carry out, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: Full adder with a carry in
exercises.brief: A full adder adds A = 1, B = 1 and a carry in of 1. What is the sum bit, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: How many select lines
exercises.brief: You want a multiplexer that can pick one of eight inputs. Explain how many select lines it needs and why, and mention one practical limit that comes with the design.

exercises.title: Setting a latch
exercises.brief: An SR latch is set (S = 1, R = 0). What is Q, as 0 or 1?

exercises.title: Why the clock edge
exercises.brief: Explain why a D flip-flop only takes its new value on the clock edge and not continuously, and say what would go wrong in a design where it changed continuously.

exercises.title: Counting up
exercises.brief: A 4-bit counter starts at 0 and is clocked once per second. What is its value after 9 seconds, as a decimal number?

exercises.title: Sampling rate
exercises.brief: You need to capture a signal with components up to 8 kHz. What is the minimum sampling rate, in kilohertz, according to the sampling theorem?

exercises.title: Why the filter has to come first
exercises.brief: Explain what aliasing is, why an anti-aliasing filter has to be placed before the converter rather than after it, and say what filter type is used.

exercises.title: The noise you cannot see
exercises.brief: Your analogue reading is noisy and drifts. Name two different sources of that noise, and say what you would change about the layout or the ground return to reduce it.

exercises.title: Loading on a line
exercises.brief: A logic output drives a 50 Ω input. What percentage of the output voltage actually appears at the input, if the output impedance is 5 Ω?

exercises.title: Build a divider
exercises.brief: Build a voltage divider: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and a resistor from node 2 to ground. Set the two resistors to 1 kΩ each, then check that the output node sits at half the supply.

exercises.title: Build an RC circuit
exercises.brief: Build an RC charging circuit: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and a capacitor from node 2 to ground. Run the simulation and watch the voltage at node 2 rise towards the supply.

exercises.title: Build an LED circuit
exercises.brief: Build an LED circuit: a battery across node 1, a resistor from node 1 to node 2, and an LED from node 2 to ground. Run the simulation and read the current through the LED.

exercises.title: Set a precision bias point
exercises.brief: Use the supplied 6 V battery and two resistors: node 1 to 2, then 2 to ground. Design for 4 V at node 2 (±0.04 V) with 2 mA source current (±0.05 mA). Your ratio must also give 2 V when the checker changes only the supply to 3 V.

exercises.title: Calibrate under load
exercises.brief: Use two resistors from 1 to 2 and 2 to ground. On 6 V design for 3.6 V unloaded and 3.0 V when an instrument connects 6 kΩ from node 2 to ground (±0.04 V). The checker attaches the instrument temporarily. Build just the divider.

exercises.title: Null a two-arm bridge
exercises.brief: Connect two divider arms from node 1 to ground with midpoints at nodes 2 and 3. On a 6 V supply both midpoints must read 4 V, their differential must be within 0.01 V of zero, and total supply current must be 3 mA (±0.05 mA). Multiple resistor combinations work.

courses.title: Systems Lab
courses.subject: Networking, cloud usage, device support, defensive security and digital signals

exercises.title: Size an IPv4 subnet
exercises.brief: A classroom needs fifty host addresses. Move from /24 to /26 and predict how many usable addresses remain in a conventional broadcast subnet.

exercises.title: Divide a switch into VLANs
exercises.brief: A switch has twelve connected access ports. One device broadcasts. Predict the number of other lab ports receiving the frame when eight ports share its VLAN.

exercises.title: Diagnose memory pressure
exercises.brief: An OS uses 3 GiB and a workload needs 7 GiB. Predict the shortfall with 8 GiB installed. Then increase memory and observe where the shortfall ends.

exercises.title: Plan a recovery image
exercises.brief: A workstation needs a 12 GiB recovery image. Predict how many whole images fit in 30 GiB, then test the next capacity threshold.

exercises.title: Drain a worker queue
exercises.brief: Start a one-second window with 15 queued jobs. Twelve more arrive, and each worker can finish six. Predict the remaining backlog with three workers.

exercises.title: Measure cache misses
exercises.brief: Serve 100 independent reads through a cache. Predict the database reads if 85 are cache hits. Assume a single origin read per miss.

exercises.title: Budget a compute workload
exercises.brief: A job runs for six hours. Predict the usage meter for five identical instances, then compare it with a smaller deployment.

exercises.title: Size a backup retention window
exercises.brief: A bucket keeps one full 4 GiB backup per day. Predict steady-state storage for seven daily copies, with no deduplication or compression.

exercises.title: Prioritize an update rollout
exercises.brief: A fleet inventory lists 24 devices needing an approved update. Predict how many still need the update after deployment succeeds on 18.

exercises.title: Test a recovery point objective
exercises.brief: A service writes ten records per hour. Estimate the worst-case records since the last successful snapshot when snapshots are four hours apart.

exercises.title: Read the least significant bit
exercises.brief: Read the eight-bit representation of sample 173. Predict the value of its rightmost bit. Compare with 172.

exercises.title: Measure samples per cycle
exercises.brief: Sample a 4 Hz sine wave at 32 Hz. Predict how many equally spaced readings fall within one cycle, then compare the shape at 8 Hz.

exercises.title: Read a classifier result
exercises.brief: Twenty samples in a validation set are positive. Predict recall when the classifier finds sixteen. Change the count and inspect the missed examples.

exercises.title: Probe a resistor divider
exercises.brief: A 12 V ideal source drives two resistors in series. The upper resistor is 1 kΩ. Predict the unloaded midpoint voltage with 3 kΩ below the probe.

exercises.title: Find the peak backlog during a burst
exercises.brief: A cold queue receives 3, 18, 20, 0, then 0 jobs over five seconds. Arrivals enter before service. Each worker finishes four jobs per second. Predict the largest end-of-second backlog with three workers. Compare the peak with the final queue.

exercises.title: Size the queue after losing a zone
exercises.brief: Three equal zones serve a steady 75 requests per second. Lose one zone for 10 seconds starting with an empty queue. Each remaining replica serves 8 requests per second. Predict the outstanding requests with four replicas per zone.

exercises.title: Locate the p95 latency cliff
exercises.brief: In a batch of 100 requests, fast responses take 30 ms and slow ones 800 ms. Predict the nearest-rank 95th percentile with six slow responses. Compare with five to find where one response changes the reported percentile.
